sourceNote: The T-pose rabbit mesh rabbit-tpose.glb (armSource, assets/models/rabbit/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist, so that the arms and the wrists do not twist. tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py makes these faces with the arms 1.18 times longer (--factor 1.18). The other faces and rabbit-tpose.glb stay unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, as on the polar bear, because the seated bind of the app depends on them.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units: twice the gap of the joint rings of arm_rebuild.py, which spans the three rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts).

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the normals of the skin with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as on the fox and the cat. Thus the seam between the upper arm and the trunk shows no hard line.
rootNormals.armShareNote: A face of the radius stays in the rim only when the mean weight of its corners on the clavicle and the arm bones of its side is 0.3 or more (root_rim()), as on the hippo. Thus the faces of the upper chest and the back keep their facets.
rootNormals.elbowNote: The faces within 0.06 units of each elbow joint take the skin normals too, as on the fox. Each hold bends the elbows, and the crease angle splits the normals of the inner elbows into hard lines.

name: Rabbit

app.note: The app puts the standing shoulder joints 0.8513179 m above the floor (ANIMALS of tools/studio-body.ts), as for the A-pose rabbit. The shoulder joints of the mesh are at 0.5945 u after the leg factor, so the scale is 1.4320 m for each unit. The reach is 0.3886 m, and the violin is 0.83 of the violin of the app.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 keeps the arm length, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms. The arms of rabbit-arms.glb are 1.18 times longer than the source arms (arm_rebuild.py --factor 1.18), and the arm joints are the joints of the longer arms. 1.18 is the smallest factor of the sweep 1, 1.1, 1.13, 1.16, 1.18, and 1.2 at which the left paw reaches the nut of the violin of 0.83 (stopRange from 0.01, as the A-pose rabbit). The reach is then 1.21 H, as the 1.22 H of the A-pose rabbit. With 1, the paw reaches the fingerboard only from 0.34.
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh, as for the A-pose rabbit. It stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises by the growth of the legs, so that the soles stay at y 0. The chair of the app fits the legs, so the soles stand on the floor.
shinFactorNote: The shin is shorter than the thigh factor makes it (13.3 cm, old A-pose rabbit 14.8 cm, 15.6 cm with 1.75), so that the hips joint of the seated bind is as high as on the A-pose rabbit (35.2 cm, old 35.5 cm, 37.8 cm with 1.75). The feet keep their places, so the layout does not change. With the deeper haunch (sit.most) and the wider thighs (legGirth), the seat is 25.0 cm high (old 26.2 cm, 33.1 cm before).
legGirthNote: The thigh of the T-pose mesh is thinner than the thigh of the A-pose rabbit, and the leg factor makes it long, so the seated thigh looked thin. The thigh takes the factor 1.6 across its axis before the skin (leg_girth() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), up and to the sides, so that its width comes near the width of the A-pose rabbit. The back of the thigh keeps its place, so the underside stays on the seat. The shin keeps its form.
neckFactorNote: The head of the T-pose mesh sat on the shoulders: the neck was 4.3 cm (A-pose rabbit 7.5 cm), and the trunk 45.9 cm (49.1 cm). The neck between its joints is 1.95 times as long as on the mesh, the trunk from the hips joint to the chest joint 1.1 times (trunkTop: the upper chest and the arm roots keep their form), and the head and the ears are 0.93 times as large, around the neck joint. So the neck is 7.8 cm, the trunk 49.0 cm, and the chin of the seated bind 7.7 cm above the shoulder tops (4.4 cm before). The export keeps the head before the factor for the holds (ungrown() of tools/studio-body.ts). With 1.75 and no head factor, the neck was 7.5 cm, but the large head still covered it from the front and the back.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The arms are level in the T-pose, and the arm joints lie on the middle line of the arm at the joints of the 1.18 times longer arms. The palm is the true palm of the source: the mean normal of the pink pads of the palm faces down.

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back until the hip angle opens by open degrees, as seated string players sit tall. The shares fall from the spine1 to the head in equal steps, so that the head stays level. The value 0 keeps the trunk of the source.
studio.bindArmsNote: With straightArms, bindArms.upper_arm sets the bind upper arm, and bindArms.forearm sets only the elbow axis: the cross product of the bind upper arm and this forearm direction (StudioBody.hinges, bind_hinges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The two directions are the directions of the bent bind of the violin hold, so that the elbow axes and the zero of the roll of the upper arm stay. The paw has no bind direction, because it keeps the turn of the upper arm.
studio.straightArmsNote: The bind keeps the arms of the source straight: the forearm and the paw keep the turn of the upper arm, so that the rest shape holds the bend of no role, and each hold bends the elbow and the wrist from the same shape (the role-neutral bind of design 4.4).
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of each arm turns about its bind forearm toward supination, the left 90 degrees and the right 43 degrees (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), and the forearm segments share the turn. Each value makes the largest paw twist p95 of the six roles of the cast matrix on the straight bind smallest (design 4.4): about 137 degrees on the left (the violin and the snare drum) and 93 degrees on the right (the cello and the snare drum). Three probes of pnpm bind-supination gave 97 and 43, then 90 and 43, then no change.
studio.note: The leg turns of the A-pose rabbit: the thighs of the T-pose mesh have the same direction, so the seat keeps its form. The shin is vertical, as the legs of the red fox.

paintedBelow.note: The weights of Blender gave the side of the trunk under each arm root only the clavicle and the arm, so the raised bow arm pulled the side up and out: the side gap of pnpm trunk-form violinist --to 0.9 was 3.4 and 6.6 cm in the play. Below y 0.52, a part of the clavicle and arm weight within 0.105 u of the middle plane goes to the trunk, all of it at y 0.4 (painted_below() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py).

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units).

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends.

weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). Thus the turns of the head do not pull the top of each shoulder.
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, so that the curl of the fingers does not turn over a face between the hand and the fingers.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the haunch stays on the seat and the thigh turns onto it. This is the ramp of the fox, scaled by the thigh of the rabbit.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail ball follows the tail only.
weights.rigidPaintedNote: The corners of each group of faces at these points take the mean of their painted weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py, after the painted weights). The points are the middles of the bridge faces under each arm root and of the first ring of the tube under it. The T-pose arm turns about 80 degrees down to hang, and these faces folded in each sample of the rest and the play (pnpm fold-probe violinist --faces).

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane and the flip moves the surface by at most move (units). The angle 180 turns the flips off.

refine.ringsNote: No ring: the quad tube of each arm of rabbit-arms.glb has 3 rings at each elbow and at each wrist.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the thin faces of the seated bind mesh near a joint of the arms or the legs as candidates for a ring (refine.rings).

tone.note: The light grey fur takes the cream of the fur swatch of rabbit-views.png (Oklab 0.938, 0.009, 0.018): each plain face moves by a row [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab, blended by its lightness. The pink nose, inner ears, and paw pads have more chroma, and the white whiskers are lighter than light, so they keep their colors.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at a grid of samples. A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples are below dark. A dark face in the eye box is an eye, and a face in the nose box near the nose color is the nose. A palette of palette colors (k-means in Oklab) keeps the colors few.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most points points of their edge, lifted along the normal of the eye. pnpm studio-body drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The faces of the old eye take the main color of the ring around it.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat. Its front edge ends where the sloped thighs leave the seat top at the haunch. The chair of the app grows back until its back posts keep 1 cm behind the trunk (backRoom of ANIMALS of tools/studio-body.ts).

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Each vertex near the seam moves share of the way to the middle of its neighbors in rounds rounds, with a weight that falls from the seam out.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch goes down onto the seat in the seated bind, with the rule of the fox (sit of tools/mesh-rigs/fox.json). The drop fades over the last 0.02 units of the haunch, where the haunch meets the tail ball, so that no face between them turns over. The haunch of the T-pose mesh ends 4.6 cm higher under the hips joint than the haunch of the A-pose rabbit, and the wide thighs (legGirth) set the seat top 5.2 cm under the haunch. So the drop can be up to 0.1 units (most), and the haunch comes down onto the seat, as on the A-pose rabbit. With 0.045, the haunch stayed 6.5 cm above the seat from the side.
